newsitem.title: USA: TWA denies board met with investor Freeman.
newsitem.headline: TWA denies board met with investor Freeman.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc, denying a news report, said Friday its board of directors has never met with investor Brian Freeman.
USA Today reported Thursday that representatives from Strategic Capital Group, which is led by investor Brian Freeman, has proposed a deal to take control of TWA.

"Brian Freeman did not meet with the board this week for the purpose of making such a proposal," TWA said in a statement. "In fact, neither Brian Freeman nor anyone representing Brian Freeman has ever met with the board."
USA Today also reported that Transaero, a Russian airline, which is part of a Strategic Capital partner, wants to use TWA as a U.S. feeder.
On Thursday, Transaero denied it was interested in taking control of TWA. "Transaero has no interest in a possible stock purchase of TWA," spokeswoman Natalia Aleksashina said.
"Our relationship with TWA can be viewed only from a position of possible cooperation in developing air routes between Russia and the United States," she added.
In its statement, TWA said that, from time to time, it receives investment proposals from various sources.
"Our usual policy is not to comment on such proposals," TWA said. "However, we feel it is necessary to correct an erroneous report in ... USA Today."
